locator.section: 8 / Detailed Mechanisms of Ion Fragmentation (Random or hidden rearrangements)

evidence.curator_note: Equation 8.7, row 3 (second bracketed ion-molecule complex -> separated products). Intra-complex hydrogen-atom transfer: the vinyloxy radical abstracts an H atom from the sec-butyl cation. Net H-atom transfer turns the sec-butyl cation into the but-2-ene radical cation C4H8+. (m/z 56) and the vinyloxy radical into neutral acetaldehyde CH3CHO. Book draws 4 arc(s): (1) the sec-butyl C-H attacking the vinyloxy terminal carbon = move 1; (2) the hook forming the butene double bond = move 2 (the book draws a full C=C; encoded here as the localized 1,2-distonic radical cation CH3-CH.-CH+-CH3 required for one-electron bookkeeping); (3) the vinyloxy C=C shifting toward the carbonyl = move 4; (4) the O odd-electron fishhook = move 5. Move 3 (the second electron completing the new C-H bond to the terminal carbon) is an implicit hook, not drawn as its own arc. DRAWN COMPLEX: reactant is the square-bracketed complex {sec-butyl cation, CH2=CH-O.}; encoded as two-species states since the complex is not a single mapped SMILES. DELOCALISATION: the page draws the butene product with a full C=C and '+.'; the localized distonic form CH3-CH.-CH+-CH3 is chosen so the arrows balance (RDKit cannot carry an overall radical cation on a closed C=C). The vinyloxy radical is drawn/encoded as the O-radical form CH2=CH-O. (same as bracket 2). Text: at LOW electron energy 'the C4H8+ ion predominates', consistent with this channel; IE(1-butene)=9.6 eV.

Cross-link (PARTIAL/NET, and the cited rule is BROKEN): MØD rule IMS_8_7_5 (rule_name 'Hydrogen exchange occring in a Ion-Molecule-Complex 8.7 row 3 process 2', IMS_chap8_examples.py:442). Its product DFS contains a MALFORMED bond token '[=}' (should be '{=}') at '[C]2[=}[C+.]3'. VERIFIED IN-CONTAINER: this does NOT raise (mod.Rule.fromDFS parses it and the module imports), so the rule is NOT dead - but MOD SILENTLY ABSORBS the bad token into a product NODE LABEL: getGMLString() shows right[ node[ id 2 label "=}[C+." ] ], a phantom non-element node. Consequently the intended C2=C3 double bond and the C+. charge/radical are LOST; the rule loads but its right-hand side does NOT encode the butene radical cation. So IMS_8_7_5 is semantically broken (a real corpus bug), independent of the fact that it is also a COLLAPSED NET rule folding steps c/d/e (distonic ion straight to C4H8+. + CH3CHO) rather than the elementary bracket-2 -> products step drawn here. Listed in rule_mismatches. Fix in the rule source: '[=}' -> '{=}'.

The text states that 'at low electron energies the C4H8+ ion predominates' (Liedtke and Djerassi 1969) -- this m/z 56 radical cation is the detected product of the low-energy complex channel. No numeric intensity is printed for it on this page, so relative_intensity is OMITTED. observed_mz 56.0621 is the curator-computed monoisotopic m/z of C4H8+. (electron-mass corrected).
